title: Learning with all my senses
examples: How can I learn spellings better?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Learn a spelling with your senses

explain.say: You can learn with your eyes, your ears and your hands. Using them together helps everyone remember. Look at the board. You will learn a spelling in 3 ways.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Learn a spelling with your senses

explain.say: The eye group is lit up. See it. Colour the word, use picture cards, or look at the shape of the word. Some letters are tall, and some are short. What colour would you make your word?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Learn a spelling with your senses

explain.say: Now look at the ear group. Hear it. Say the word out loud. Clap the beats. Sing it to a tune. Hearing the word helps you remember it. Can you clap your name?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Learn a spelling with your senses

explain.say: Look at the hand. Touch and move. Write the word in sand. Build it with letter tiles. Or skywrite it with big letters in the air. Can you skywrite the word cat with me?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Learn a spelling with your senses

explain.say: Now try the word sunset. Look at it. Say it. Clap it: sun, set. That is 2 claps. Then skywrite it. You used your eyes, ears and hands. This week, learn one spelling in all 3 ways.

faq.a: It means learning with more than one sense at once, like seeing, saying and writing a word together. It helps you remember.

faq.q: How can seeing help me spell?
faq.a: Colours, pictures and word shapes give your brain a picture of the word to remember.

faq.q: How can hearing help me spell?
faq.a: Saying a word aloud, clapping its beats or singing it uses your ears. Hearing the word gives you one more way to remember it.
Skywriting means writing big letters in the air with your straight arm. Your muscles help you remember the shape.
asks: Tell me about Touch and move

faq.q: Which sense is best for me?
faq.a: Using them together works best for everyone. Seeing, saying and writing a word helps you remember it. A grown-up you trust can help you try.

facts: Sunset has two syllables: sun and set.
Using sight, sound and movement together is called multisensory learning.

quiz.say: Say the word sunset. Clap each beat. How many claps?
quiz.why: Sun, set. That is 2 beats, so 2 claps.

wrong.0: Say it slowly, sun then set, and you hear 2 beats.
wrong.2: Sunset has 2 beats: sun and set.

quiz.say: Amira writes her spelling word in sand. Which group is this?
quiz.show: Amira writes her word in sand. Which group?
quiz.why: Writing in sand uses Amira's hands and movement.

wrong.0: See it uses your eyes, like colouring the word.
wrong.1: Hear it uses your ears, like singing the word.
